summary.text: Phil Steck is a Democratic member of the New York State Assembly who has represented District 110 since 2013 and is seeking re-election on the Working Families Party and Democratic lines in the November 3, 2026 general election; he is an employment and civil rights attorney.

paragraphs.text: Steck earned a high school diploma from Albany Academy, a bachelor's degree in government from Harvard University and a J.D. from the University of Pennsylvania in 1984.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he served as an assistant district attorney in New York and Rensselaer Counties from 1987 to 1989, joined the law firm Cooper, Erving and Savage LLP in 1990, and concentrates his practice on civil rights and employment law.
He was elected to the Albany County Legislature in 1999 and re-elected three times.
Steck won the Assembly seat in 2012, taking office on January 1, 2013, and Ballotpedia lists him as chair of the Alcoholism and Drug Abuse Committee.

In the same survey, he said his campaign messages include addressing rising utility prices through state investment in the power grid, ending corporate subsidies, and ending the subminimum wage for disabled workers.
